chunk_findings.detail: The unconditional `"approvals": len(data.get("approvals_pending", ()))` is still placed in the dict that is then passed to `return O.ok("status", **data)`. With no pending approval request, `data` has no `approvals_pending` list, so the returned status payload still contains `"approvals": 0`, contradicting the new behavior that “only when a request waits” and the test named `test_the_brief_and_status_say_nothing_until_a_request_waits`. The triage says this key sits under `_render`, which is never on the wire, but the diff hunk does not show any `_render` assignment or rendering indirection between this dict and the `return O.ok(...)` line, so that probe does not answer the finding.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/reporting/overview.py:273

chunk_findings.detail: The new config value is written as the TOML literal string `'8'`, so an applied upgrade puts a string into `approvals.min_digest_chars` instead of the integer `8`. This key is a count of digest characters used in comparisons/slicing, so once a person tries `ddflow approvals approve`/`deny` the code will compare an `int` to a `str` (or slice with a `str`) and raise `TypeError`. It should be the unquoted integer `new = 8`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/knob_added.approvals.min_digest_chars.toml:6

chunk_findings.detail: This adds `"revoked"` as a required field to the already existing `ask.withdrawn` event kind while leaving `"v": 1`. A pre-change v1 event such as `{"kind":"ask.withdrawn","fields":{"by":"agent:alice","id":"Q1"},"v":1}` is no longer valid under the v1 schema during replay/validation because it lacks `revoked`. The event version should be bumped to `2`, or `revoked` should be optional/defaulted, to keep existing v1 events readable.
chunk_findings.title: tests/fixtures/event_kinds.json:82

chunk_findings.detail: The regression test named `test_no_mcp_tool_carries_the_approvals_verbs` does not actually inspect the surface registry for approval tools: after importing `registry`, the only assertion is `assert registry is not None`. A successful import already guarantees the name is not `None`, so a registry that does carry an `approvals_approve` MCP tool still passes this check. The test would need to examine the registry’s discovered tool names instead; as written it is a tautology for the exact exposure it claims to prevent.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_approvals_cli.py:175

chunk_findings.detail: The test claims `brief` and `status` say nothing until a request waits, but before filing the request it never runs the plain human-readable `status` command; it only checks `brief` and `--json status` (asserting only that `approvals_pending` is absent). Plain `status` is first asserted at line 43, after `filed` already exists. Therefore an implementation where `ddflow status` always prints `approval request(s) waiting for the operator`—or where JSON status always includes an approvals summary—still passes this test. Failing input: no pending approvals plus a human `status` renderer that unconditionally emits the approval line; the “nothing until a request waits” behavior is not actually enforced.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_approvals_pending_line.py:32-44

chunk_findings.detail: The new regression test passes `--digest "zzzzzzzz"`, which is exactly the default `approvals.min_digest_chars` value of `8`. In `ddflow/api/approvals_answer.py`, the changed `O.refused(...)` message (the branch that used to end with `({shown[:16]}...)`) is emitted only when the supplied digest is shorter than that minimum, so this call takes the `AN.answer` path instead of the modified refusal branch. Consequently, reverting the changed production line to include the leaked digest prefix would still leave this test passing; the test does not exercise the code it is meant to protect.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_approvals_cli.py:test_an_answer_with_a_wrong_digest_does_not_print_the_right_one

Fix: refuse unless outcome is approved; regression test: deny then revoke -> refused, status stays denied. Found by roborev on RA-cli; deferred to avoid a second multi-hour ci queue.

data.body:
Fixes bug B1018a598b1: ddflow approvals revoke on a DENIED ask is accepted and flips its status from denied to withdrawn (engine.revoke checks state == answered, not outcome == approved). Fix: refuse unless outcome is approved; regression test: deny then revoke -> refused, status stays denied. Found by roborev on RA-cli; deferred to avoid a second multi-hour ci queue.

Write the regression test first and watch it FAIL on the unfixed code; then `ddflow complete fix-B1018a598b1 --regression-test <test>` closes the bug with the task (or `ddflow bug fixed B1018a598b1 --regression-test <test>` first).

chunk_findings.detail: The function’s return contract changes from `O.Outcome | None` to `(O.Outcome | None, dict)`, but its caller in `record` (same file) is not updated by this diff and still treats the result as a single `O.Outcome`. Every non-refusal path now returns `(None, {})`. For example, a normal person gate record such as `record(repo, item="pkg", gate="review", agent="", hard_skip=False, hand=False)` returns `(None, {})` instead of `None`. Since a non-empty tuple is truthy, an existing `if refusal := _agent_skip_refusal(...):` or `if ... is not None` check incorrectly sees it as a refusal, or returns a tuple where an `O.Outcome` is expected downstream. It also never forwards the approval stamp to `_evidence_fields`, so the intended `evidence.approval` is not attached when an agent’s approval is spent.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/gates.py:_agent_skip_refusal

chunk_findings.detail: The second modified command (the hand-recorded outcome command) declares `Param("approval")` and tries to read it via `a.get("approval")`, but, unlike the first command at line 602, it does not add `"approval"` to that command's record-field tuple. So a valid override such as calling this command with `--approval Q123` over a failed review gate will produce a record whose approval evidence is absent from the durable record, violating the change's requirement that the record carry `evidence.approval`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/declared/lifecycle.py:633 (and :667)

chunk_findings.detail: The helper extracts the ask id by splitting `err` on the substring `"approval "`, but the refusal message this same file asserts contains `"operator's"` will normally read like `"operator's approval is required; re-run with --approval Q123"`. `err.split("approval ", 1)` then matches the `"approval "` after `"operator's"`, so `[1]` starts with `"is required; ..."` and `word` becomes `"is"`, failing `assert word.startswith("Q")`. This breaks `test_an_agent_is_refused_and_the_refusal_files_the_request` and every other test using `_refusal_id` before the feature is exercised. Split on `"--approval "` instead, or parse `--approval\s+(\S+)`.

data.body:
After RA-consume-gate-skip: each Site row in services/approvals/sites.py gets its canonical command, state digest and --approval flag; the agent_marker refusal becomes operator_gate; family B verbs (upgrade --self, plan confirm, skew override) accept --approval and keep relayed consent for one release with a doctor warning on each relayed use (D-RA-Q2); forced complete/claim gated (D-RA-Q7). Tests per site as in tests/test_approvals_consume.py.

Also (from roborev on RA-consume-gate-skip): a provider and a test for a HAND-RECORDED unavailable/partial/passed over CONFIRMED findings (args outcome), and let 'approvals request' take the outcome.

chunk_findings.detail: The function only refuses when the row is missing or has no verb and when `accept_harness` is off; it never checks the request level. The intent and the new knob both say this channel is “T2 only” (level 2 only). Given a pending `ask_id` whose state row has `level` 0 or 1 and `accept_harness=True`, `approvals_ask` returns `O.ok` and prints the AskUserQuestion payload, telling the agent to use the harness channel for a non-T2 request. That either results in a non-T2 approval being attestable from a transcript (if attest also misses the check) or an honest-author trap where `approvals ask` succeeds and the later `approvals attest` refuses.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/approvals_harness.py:approvals_ask

chunk_findings.detail: The decision and the recorded event each call `E.verified_level(row, cfg)` separately: first inside `_problem` at line 70, then again when appending the spend event at line 107. With the new harness verifier, that verified level is only trustworthy while the external harness transcript still contains the answer row, and the `log.transaction()` lock does not lock those transcript files. Given ask_id `a` with `min_level=2`, if the harness transcript row exists when `_problem` runs but is removed or rotated (or rewritten by the same uid) before line 107, the first call returns L2 and `_problem` passes, while the second call returns a lower level such as L0. The spend event is still appended and the call succeeds, even though the answer was accepted after the transcript no longer holds it, violating the stated harness guarantee.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/approvals/consume.py:spend (lines 70 and 107)

chunk_findings.detail: `verify` relies on `find`, which returns only the newest `Attested` for the question (`return hits[-1]`). If the transcript still contains the recorded proof `T1`, but a later accepted answer to the same question text is appended with a different tool_use id `T2`, `find` returns `T2` and `verify` returns `False`. For example, recorded row has `proof="toolu_1"` / `outcome=APPROVED`; the transcript has an older accepted `toolu_1` row and a later accepted `toolu_2` row for the same `row["text"]`; `verify` sees `toolu_2 != toolu_1` and reports the recorded answer invalid, even though `toolu_1` is still present. That contradicts the verifier's own stated contract that the proof tool_use id still be there with the same answer.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/approvals/harness.py:verify

chunk_findings.detail: Inserting `proof: str = ""` before the existing `now: float | None = None` changes the positional argument contract. A previously valid positional call such as `answer(log, cfg, kind, ask_id, answer, actor, "cli", 1, 1234.5)` used `1234.5` as `now`; after this change `1234.5` is bound to `proof` and `now` becomes `None`, so the answer is recorded with the wrong timestamp/proof value. New optional arguments added to an existing function must go after `now`, or existing positional callers must be migrated.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ask/engine.py answer()

chunk_findings.detail: The new `"ask"` entry is `("id", "input")`, but `ddflow/surfaces/declared/approvals.py` declares `approvals ask` with only `Param("id")`, and `cmd_approvals_ask` only reads `a.id` and never passes an `input` value to `AH.approvals_ask`. This is a disagreement between the command argument table and the declared command contract: a parser or binder driven by this table can make the documented one-argument invocation fail for a second positional `input`, or expose/accept an `input` token that is silently ignored. It should be `("id",)`.

chunk_findings.detail: `spend` now makes `verified_level` depend on mutable harness transcript state, but it evaluates that state twice: once inside `_problem` to decide whether the approval holds, and again when writing the spend event. These calls are not against the log lock’s protected data, so a T2 harness row can pass the first check and then stop passing before the second. Example: ask `a1` has `min_level=2`, `row["via"]="harness"`, and its transcript row exists during `_problem`, so `_problem` returns `""`; a transcript cleanup process removes that row before line 107, so the second `E.verified_level(row, cfg)` returns a lower level. `spend` then appends an approval use with `level=1` and returns success for a request that no longer holds at L2. The level should be computed once inside the transaction and reused for both the check and the recorded event.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/approvals/consume.py:107

chunk_findings.detail: `_accepted` reads the wrong `permissionDecision` field. A normal harness-written accepted `AskUserQuestion` result places a string `"accept"` inside `toolUseResult` (`row["toolUseResult"]["permissionDecision"]`), not a top-level object with a nested `"decision"` key. For such a row, `(row.get("permissionDecision") or {}).get("decision")` evaluates to `None`, so `ok` is false and `_accepted` returns `""`. Concrete input: `{"type":"user","uuid":"u2","sourceToolAssistantUUID":"u1","toolUseResult":{"permissionDecision":"accept","answers":{"Ask [ask1] ...":"Approve ask1"}},"message":{"content":[{"type":"tool_result","tool_use_id":"tu1"}]}}` is not recognized, and `attest` reports “no answer”.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/approvals/harness.py:102

chunk_findings.detail: `verify` calls `find`, which returns the latest accepted answer for the request’s question (`hits[-1]`), and then requires that hit’s `tool_use_id` to equal the stored `row["proof"]`. If a newer duplicate accepted answer for the exact same question is appended after the approval was recorded, the recorded proof row is still present but `find` returns the newer `tool_use_id`, so `verify` returns false and invalidates a previously valid L2 approval. Example transcript: `tu1` accepted and recorded, later `tu2` accepted for the same question; `verify` sees `tu2 != tu1` and fails even though `tu1` still exists.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/approvals/harness.py:152

chunk_findings.detail: `proof: str = ""` is inserted before the existing `now: float | None = None` parameter, so any existing positional call that passes `now` after `level` now binds that value to `proof` and leaves `now` unset. For example, `engine.answer(log, cfg, "Q1", "yes", "", None, "", "", "cli", 1, 1234567890.0)` now records `proof=1234567890.0` and defaults `now` to the current time; the returned answer row has a corrupted proof field and the caller-supplied timestamp is lost. New optional parameters must be appended after `now` or made keyword-only.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ask/engine.py:answer

chunk_findings.detail: The assertion `(q["question"] == row["text"] and row["id"] in row["text"]) or row["digest"][:16] in row["text"]` makes `q["question"] == row["text"]` skippable. For any request whose rendered `row["text"]` contains its digest prefix (`row["digest"][:16]`), a broken `H.payload` that returns `"question": "corrupted"` still makes the second operand True, so the test passes despite not printing the rendered request text. The parentheses should be `q["question"] == row["text"] and (row["id"] in row["text"] or row["digest"][:16] in row["text"])`.

chunk_findings.detail: `verify` calls `find`, which returns the latest accepted answer for the request’s question (`hits[-1]`), and then requires that hit’s `tool_use_id` to equal the stored `row["proof"]`. If a newer duplicate accepted answer for the exact same question is appended after the approval was recorded, the recorded proof row is still present but `find` returns the newer `tool_use_id`, so `verify` returns false and invalidates a previously valid L2 approval. Example transcript: `tu1` accepted and recorded, later `tu2` accepted for the same question; `verify` sees `tu2 != tu1` and fails even though `tu1` still exists.

chunk_findings.detail: `proof: str = ""` is inserted before the existing `now: float | None = None` parameter, so any existing positional call that passes `now` after `level` now binds that value to `proof` and leaves `now` unset. chunk_findings.detail: The function only refuses when the row is missing or has no verb and when `accept_harness` is off; it never checks the request level. The intent and the new knob both say this channel is “T2 only” (level 2 only). Given a pending `ask_id` whose state row has `level` 0 or 1 and `accept_harness=True`, `approvals_ask` returns `O.ok` and prints the AskUserQuestion payload, telling the agent to use the harness channel for a non-T2 request. That either results in a non-T2 approval being attestable from a transcript (if attest also misses the check) or an honest-author trap where `approvals ask` succeeds and the later `approvals attest` refuses.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/approvals_harness.py:approvals_ask

chunk_findings.detail: The decision and the recorded event each call `E.verified_level(row, cfg)` separately: first inside `_problem` at line 70, then again when appending the spend event at line 107. With the new harness verifier, that verified level is only trustworthy while the external harness transcript still contains the answer row, and the `log.transaction()` lock does not lock those transcript files. Given ask_id `a` with `min_level=2`, if the harness transcript row exists when `_problem` runs but is removed or rotated (or rewritten by the same uid) before line 107, the first call returns L2 and `_problem` passes, while the second call returns a lower level such as L0. The spend event is still appended and the call succeeds, even though the answer was accepted after the transcript no longer holds it, violating the stated harness guarantee.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/approvals/consume.py:spend (lines 70 and 107)

chunk_findings.detail: `verify` relies on `find`, which returns only the newest `Attested` for the question (`return hits[-1]`). If the transcript still contains the recorded proof `T1`, but a later accepted answer to the same question text is appended with a different tool_use id `T2`, `find` returns `T2` and `verify` returns `False`. For example, recorded row has `proof="toolu_1"` / `outcome=APPROVED`; the transcript has an older accepted `toolu_1` row and a later accepted `toolu_2` row for the same `row["text"]`; `verify` sees `toolu_2 != toolu_1` and reports the recorded answer invalid, even though `toolu_1` is still present. That contradicts the verifier's own stated contract that the proof tool_use id still be there with the same answer.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/approvals/harness.py:verify

chunk_findings.detail: Inserting `proof: str = ""` before the existing `now: float | None = None` changes the positional argument contract. A previously valid positional call such as `answer(log, cfg, kind, ask_id, answer, actor, "cli", 1, 1234.5)` used `1234.5` as `now`; after this change `1234.5` is bound to `proof` and `now` becomes `None`, so the answer is recorded with the wrong timestamp/proof value. New optional arguments added to an existing function must go after `now`, or existing positional callers must be migrated.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ask/engine.py answer()

chunk_findings.detail: The new `"ask"` entry is `("id", "input")`, but `ddflow/surfaces/declared/approvals.py` declares `approvals ask` with only `Param("id")`, and `cmd_approvals_ask` only reads `a.id` and never passes an `input` value to `AH.approvals_ask`. This is a disagreement between the command argument table and the declared command contract: a parser or binder driven by this table can make the documented one-argument invocation fail for a second positional `input`, or expose/accept an `input` token that is silently ignored. It should be `("id",)`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/commands/approvals.py:16

chunk_findings.detail:
The CLI test writes its config override with
`cfgfile.write_text(cfgfile.read_text() + f'\n[approvals]\ntranscript_dirs = ["{projects}"]\n')`
while `projects` is a `pathlib.Path`. On Windows, `str(projects)` contains backslashes
(e.g. `C:\Users\runner\AppData\Local\Temp\...`). In a TOML basic string, backslash introduces
an escape sequence; `\U` is an invalid Unicode escape unless followed by hex digits. The next
`run_cli(repo, "--json", "approvals", "ask", ...)` therefore fails to parse the project config
instead of returning code 0, so `assert code == 0` fails under Windows.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_approvals_harness.py:test_ask_and_attest_over_the_cli

chunk_findings.detail: The TOML-escape fix is still not valid for every legitimate temp path. `json.dumps(str(projects))` uses `ensure_ascii=True`, so a path containing a non-BMP Unicode character (for example `--basetemp` or `TMPDIR` pointing inside a directory named with an emoji such as `😀`) is serialized in the TOML string as a surrogate pair: `"\ud83d\ude00"`. TOML Unicode escapes must be Unicode scalar values, so surrogate escapes make `run_cli(repo, "--json", "approvals", "ask", ...)` fail while parsing the config. Use a TOML literal string/single-quoted form (or otherwise avoid JSON surrogate-pair escaping) if this test is meant to be path-portable.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_approvals_harness.py:216

chunk_findings.detail: The new config line writes `transcript_dirs = ['{projects}']` as a TOML single-quoted literal string. That is not valid for every legitimate pytest temp directory: if `tmp_path` contains a single quote (e.g. `TMPDIR=/tmp/ci's-tests` or `pytest --basetemp='/tmp/o'brien-tests'`), the resulting TOML literal contains an unescaped `'` and the subsequent `run_cli(repo, "--json", "approvals", "ask", ...)` fails while parsing `config.toml`. The path is still environment-dependent, so the test is not robust to a valid basetemp.

How to prevent such orphan processes to happen and to stale the work?

data.body: Operator asked how to prevent orphaned suites that starve the queue. Ba3b7509530 (watcher kills the group) and DX-orphaned-ci-suite-reaper (doctor names leftovers) cover the process-group case. A cgroup/scope also catches children that left the group (setsid, forkserver workers) and enforces a wall-clock cap independent of the owner. Detect systemd-run --user --scope; knob [ci].suite_scope = auto|off|required; record the scope name in the gate evidence; doctor names scopes. Never kill a live owner's suite.
data.title: Run each ci/unit_tests suite in a transient systemd user scope (or cgroup) with a hard RuntimeMax and kill-on-owner-exit, falling back to the process-group watcher where systemd-run is unavailable

data.body: A session-level pytest plugin (loaded only by ddflow ci run via an env var holding the owner pid and a deadline) polls the owner pid and the deadline and aborts the session, so a suite cannot outlive its gate run even without the watcher or a scope. Add an overall deadline (the per-test --timeout=420 does not bound the whole run). Test: owner killed mid-run, suite exits within N seconds; deadline reached, suite exits with the recorded reason.
data.title: Suite-side watchdog: the pytest session exits when its owning ddflow ci run is gone or past an overall deadline

Should ddflow intercept sigchld and sigint and sigterm and sighup to manage the orphan processes?

data.body: Answer to the operator's question whether ddflow should intercept SIGCHLD/SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP. Yes for TERM/INT/HUP in the entry points that own a child (gate runner, ci run): set a flag in the handler, then in the main loop forward the signal to the child process group, wait a grace period, SIGKILL the group, record the gate unavailable with 'terminated by SIGNAL', release the suite lock, restore the default handler and re-raise. Never install handlers when ddflow runs as a library/thread inside a host process; detached 'ddflow job run' jobs keep surviving SIGHUP on purpose. SIGKILL and OOM cannot be caught: keep the watcher (Ba3b7509530) and add prctl(PR_SET_PDEATHSIG) as a cheap belt (caveat: it fires on parent THREAD exit; set it from the owning thread). Do not handle SIGCHLD globally (interferes with subprocess/asyncio); use waitpid on owned children. In the long-lived MCP worker set PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER so orphaned grandchildren reparent to it and doctor can name/reap them. Tests: TERM/INT/HUP each leave no process and record the reason; KILL of the owner leaves no process via the watcher.
data.title: Command runner: handle SIGTERM/SIGINT/SIGHUP by forwarding to the child group and recording the gate unavailable; PR_SET_PDEATHSIG on Linux; PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER in the long-lived MCP worker

<result>**Merged to main and completed:** `GP-research` (docs-only; the standards gate is recorded `unavailable`, since there was no code to run roborev on). No separate reviewer gate ran on this docs-only pipeline. The proposal is unreviewed, so the 4-5 review rounds were not used. Your words went in via `ddflow session prompt --text`. Docs:
- `docs/ddflow/research/graded-policies.md`
- `docs/ddflow/decisions/graded-policies.md` (proposal state)

**What exists:**
- **Strength vocabularies:** six, none shared. Guidance has `enforcement` advisory|warn|block, requirements have MUST/SHOULD/MAY, principles have `override` none|waive|deviate, `[enforce]` has block|warn|off, org policy has enforce|audit, and `gates.required` is a list. The mappings live only in decision text.
- **Layering and waivers:** layering is `D-config-layer-order`, with about five separate tighten-only combiners designed. `guidance/waivers.py` is built (90-day cap, glob-scoped, person-approved by digest) but nothing calls it.
- **Checks engine:** `guidance/checks.py` is built, three-valued, with `unavailable` never a pass. No check kind is registered and nothing calls it. Checks only combine as AND; there is no any-of or at-least-k anywhere in ddflow.
- **Duplicates:** two charters (rules and requirements), three check dialects, and several ad hoc waivers.
- **Open work:** the requirements, org-config, goals and approvals phases are all still open, so this design extends them rather than adding to them.

**Design:**
- **Scale:** info, recommended, best-practice, required, forbidden. It is a derived view of `enforcement` x `override`. Best-practice is warn + deviate: comply or explain, and `complete` refuses until answered. Required is block + waive. Forbidden is required with negative polarity. "Locked" (override none) and `mode` audit|enforce are layer and mode properties, not extra levels.
- **Any-of:** a record gets named `options` (existing check kinds plus thin bridges: gate, config, tool, evidence, approval) and `satisfied_by` = `all` | `any` | `at_least k of`, nestable two levels deep. Evaluation is Kleene three-valued: `unavailable` never satisfies an `any`, and a real fail in an `all` is never masked. Results name the satisfied option and every option tried, with reasons.
- **Layering:** a lower layer may raise strength, narrow options, raise k or turn `any` into `all`. It may not lower strength, add an alternative to a company `any`, lower k or move enforce to audit. Refused at write (exit 3), ignored and reported on a hand edit.
- **Waivers:** the single `SE-waiver` record. T2 approval, 90-day cap, locked policy not waivable by a project. Unattended, required files a request and completion stays refused; best-practice deviates with a logged reason.
- **Surfaces:** brief has counts by strength plus required and forbidden lines inline. MCP gets no new tool: the actions fold into the existing `rule` family.

**Options compared:** (A) fields on the existing guidance record, recommended; (B) a new policy kind, which contradicts `D-requirements-model`; (C) config-knob-only, which cannot express alternatives of behaviour; (D) an external engine such as OPA, which adds a dependency. Rollout is audit-first. It is invalidated if the requirement kind cannot be adapted to the guidance record, if `RQM-check` slips and leaves the checks engine uncalled, if five words confuse operators, if any-of gets used to reach the weakest option, or if the required charter outgrows its cap.

**Queued:** phase `P-graded-policies`, related to P-org-config, P-requirements, P-goals, P-commit-messages, P-remote-approvals, P-deprecation, P-batch-gates, P-shared-engines and P-tool-diet. chunk_findings.detail: The `chore.approve` site still describes the approval scope as `"the current [chore].globs"`, but the new canonical constructor `ddflow/services/approvals/grant_site.py:31` now digests both `[chore].globs` and `skip_gates`. chunk_findings.detail: The hand-written-answer check calls `E.judge(r, r["digest"])`, but `r["digest"]` is the request digest, not the actual answer/proof that must be verified. An answered approval still has its request digest even when the answer has no proof, so this call never inspects the proof source and the required “approved answer without proof” finding is missed. Failing input: an `ANSWERED`/`APPROVED` record with `digest="sha256:abc"` and no answer proof reaches `E.judge(r, "sha256:abc")`; the answer/proof field is never examined.

chunk_findings.detail: `from ..ask import engine as E` resolves to `ddflow.services.ask`, one package above this file. The approvals engine this code needs (`E.APPROVED`, `E.status`, `E.judge`, `E.verified_level`) is the sibling module in the same package, `ddflow.services.approvals.ask`, so the import should be `from .ask import engine as E`. With this import, `import ddflow.services.approvals.audit` raises `ModuleNotFoundError` (or imports the wrong module), so `ddflow approvals log` cannot run at all.
